storyline.headline: New decision framework aims to protect Southern Rocky Mountain amphibians
storyline.summary: Researchers developed a decision-making framework to help resource managers combat threats to amphibians in the Southern Rocky Mountains, including chytrid fungus disease, habitat loss, and drought.

storyline.headline: SEC to Hold Roundtable on Trade-Through Rules
storyline.summary: The SEC announced it will convene a roundtable discussion focused on trade-through prohibitions, a market structure rule affecting equity trade execution.

storyline.headline: US Enacts GENIUS Act to Regulate Stablecoins
storyline.summary: The US has enacted the GENIUS Act, providing regulatory clarity for the stablecoin market and potentially expanding access to the dollar economy globally. This move is expected to bolster the dollar's status as the global reserve currency and lead to increased demand for US Treasuries.

storyline.headline: Washington Hunting Guide and Company Plead Guilty to Lacey Act Violation
storyline.summary: Branden Trager and his company Mayhem Services LLC pleaded guilty in federal court in Tacoma to violating the Lacey Act related to illegal hunting/guiding activity.

storyline.headline: Weekly Veterans Job Listings Posted
storyline.summary: A recurring post shares veteran-focused job listings for the week of July 21, 2025.

storyline.headline: VA Research Advances
storyline.summary: The VA's Office of Research and Development published findings on combating loneliness, Parkinson's disease, and asthma medication through research advances.

storyline.headline: Interior Department launches critical minerals recovery from mine waste
storyline.summary: The Department of the Interior is starting an initiative to recover critical minerals from mine waste, coal refuse, tailings and abandoned uranium mines, citing USGS research on promising sources. Secretary Doug Burgum framed the effort as boosting economic strength, national defense, and energy security.

storyline.headline: EPA Opens $14M Funding for Brownfields Job Training Grants
storyline.summary: EPA announced a Notice of Funding Opportunity for up to $14 million in FY2026 Brownfields Job Training Grants, aimed at helping communities train workers for environmental remediation jobs.

storyline.headline: EPA Awards $1M to Flint Hills Regional Council for Brownfields Revolving Loan Fund
storyline.summary: The EPA awarded $1 million to the Flint Hills Regional Council for their Brownfields Revolving Loan Fund selection. This funding aims to support the revitalization of contaminated sites in the region.

storyline.headline: Lebanese National Sentenced to 44 Months for Illegally Exporting U.S. Drill Rigs to Iran
storyline.summary: Brian Assi was sentenced to 44 months in prison for conspiring to violate U.S. sanctions laws by attempting to export American-made drill rigs to Iran.

storyline.headline: HHS, FDA and USDA Target Health Risks of Ultra-Processed Foods
storyline.summary: Federal health and agriculture agencies announced efforts to address the health risks associated with ultra-processed foods.

storyline.headline: NASA Tests 5G Networks to Support Future Air Taxi Operations
storyline.summary: NASA's Glenn Research Center built radio systems to evaluate whether 5G cellular technology can meet the communication demands of emerging air taxi aviation.

storyline.headline: BLS Releases Q2 Usual Weekly Earnings Report for Wage and Salary Workers
storyline.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics published its routine quarterly news release on usual weekly earnings of wage and salary workers.

storyline.headline: Fire Response at Lake Powell
storyline.summary: A fire response is impacting Lake Powell, with visitors advised to use caution. The situation is being monitored by Glen Canyon National Recreation Area authorities.

storyline.headline: EPA Reaffirms Indian Policy
storyline.summary: The EPA Administrator reaffirmed the EPA Policy for the Administration of Environmental Programs on Indian Reservations. This policy aims to protect the environment and public health in Indian Reservations.

storyline.headline: US Sanctions Houthi Petroleum and Financial Network
storyline.summary: The State Department sanctioned two individuals and five entities for importing refined petroleum products and evading sanctions to support Iran-backed Houthi forces, who threaten vital shipping lanes.

storyline.headline: Social Security Expands Multi-Channel Customer Service
storyline.summary: The Social Security Administration reports progress in serving customers through online, phone, and in-person channels.

storyline.headline: Landsat Program Marks 53rd Anniversary of Landsat 1 Launch
storyline.summary: NASA and USGS science communication teams published a retrospective celebrating the 53rd anniversary of the Landsat 1 satellite launch, highlighting the program's long-running Earth observation legacy.

storyline.headline: Federal Student Loan Program Provisions Take Effect
storyline.summary: The Federal Student Loan Program provisions under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act have taken effect as of enactment.

storyline.headline: USGS Landsat 9 Archive Surpasses One Million Products
storyline.summary: The USGS EROS Center's Landsat 9 archive has surpassed one million Level-1 products, representing over 1 billion megabytes of Earth observation data.

storyline.headline: Flow Photo Explorer used to study Penobscot River Basin flows
storyline.summary: An Environmental Monitor article highlights the Flow Photo Explorer tool being used to study flow dynamics in Maine's Penobscot River Basin, which affect chemical and physical processes in aquatic ecosystems.

storyline.headline: NASA Profiles Contracting Specialist Catherine Staggs' Role in Artemis Program
storyline.summary: NASA published a profile of Catherine Staggs, a contracting expert at Johnson Space Center, highlighting her work supporting the Artemis program.

storyline.headline: NPS releases print-at-home Junior Ranger book for Ice Age Trail
storyline.summary: The National Park Service made a print-at-home Junior Ranger activity booklet available for the Ice Age National Scenic Trail.

storyline.headline: HHS, FDA Applaud Food Industry Pledge to Drop Artificial Dyes
storyline.summary: HHS and FDA praised the Consumer Brands Association's commitment to remove petroleum-based FD&C artificial colors from the U.S. food supply, part of the administration's broader food safety push.

storyline.headline: US Announces Withdrawal from UNESCO
storyline.summary: The United States informed UNESCO's Director-General that it is withdrawing from the organization, citing conflicts with US national interests and opposition to UNESCO's focus on divisive social causes and UN Sustainable Development Goals.

storyline.headline: Weir Farm Artist Collective Exhibit
storyline.summary: An exhibit featuring 30 Weir Farm Artist Collective members was held at the Kershner Gallery in Weir Farm National Historical Park.

storyline.headline: US Nationals Released from Venezuela
storyline.summary: The US welcomes home ten Americans who were detained in Venezuela, thanks to President Trump's leadership. This release marks a significant development in the country's history of detaining US nationals.

storyline.headline: US Congratulates Colombia on Independence Day
storyline.summary: The US government congratulated the people of Colombia on their Independence Day, reflecting on shared ideals of liberty and justice. This diplomatic gesture highlights the historical ties between the two nations.

storyline.headline: USPS Introduces Schooner Stamped Card
storyline.summary: The U.S. Postal Service has introduced a new schooner stamped card, featuring a two-masted schooner, designed for convenient postcard mailing with attached paid postage. This new card was issued at the Minnesota Stamp Expo on July 18, 2025.

storyline.headline: NASA-Derived Textiles Featured in Tour de France
storyline.summary: A company is using NASA-derived textiles to create adaptive gear for Tour de France athletes, helping them stay comfortable in various environments.

storyline.headline: FEMA Aid Deadline Nears for Tennessee Storm Survivors
storyline.summary: Tennesseans affected by the April 2-24 severe storms, tornadoes and flooding have until Aug. 19 to apply for FEMA assistance, with Disaster Recovery Centers adjusting their hours to help with applications.

storyline.headline: DOJ Opens Second Civil Rights Probe into George Mason University
storyline.summary: The Justice Department's Civil Rights Division launched a new investigation into George Mason University over alleged racial or national origin discrimination in violation of Title VI, marking its second such probe into the school.

storyline.headline: VA's Nursing Home to Home program helps Veterans return to community living
storyline.summary: The VA's Nursing Home to Home program has helped 61 Veterans, including 92-year-old Henry White, transition from nursing homes back into their own homes or community-based settings.

storyline.headline: VA Wellness Program Promotes Yin Meditation for Stillness
storyline.summary: A Live Whole Health episode encourages veterans to pause from daily busyness and find inner stillness through Yin Meditation.

storyline.headline: Treasury Delays Anti-Money Laundering Rule for Investment Advisers to 2028
storyline.summary: FinCEN announced it will postpone the effective date of the Investment Adviser AML/CFT Program and SAR filing rule from January 2026 to January 2028, while it revisits the rule's scope through further rulemaking. Exemptive relief and a final rule delaying the effective date followed in subsequent updates.

storyline.headline: SEC Names George Botic Acting Chair of PCAOB
storyline.summary: The SEC appointed George Botic as Acting Chair of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board, filling a leadership role at the audit regulator.

storyline.headline: Bessent Calls for Overhaul of Bank Capital Rules to Boost Community Banks
storyline.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged the Federal Reserve to reform financial regulation, criticizing outdated capital requirements and pushing for changes that protect community banks and reduce regulatory burden. He outlined Treasury's plan to lead interagency efforts on banking, digital assets, and financial regulatory policy.

storyline.headline: NASA Student SUITS Challenge Concludes at Johnson Space Center
storyline.summary: Over 100 students from 12 U.S. universities showcased spacesuit and rover interface designs at NASA's Johnson Space Center, wrapping up the SUITS challenge.

storyline.headline: Indianapolis CPA Sentenced in Illegal Tax Shelter Scheme
storyline.summary: An Indiana CPA received a three-year prison sentence for helping clients file false tax returns tied to an illegal tax shelter.

storyline.headline: VA Travel Reimbursement
storyline.summary: The VA reimburses eligible Veterans and caregivers for travel costs related to health care appointments, with online filing being the easiest and fastest way to receive reimbursement.

storyline.headline: Vessel Grounds at Cape Hatteras National Seashore
storyline.summary: A vessel ran aground south of off-road vehicle ramp 38 at Cape Hatteras National Seashore, according to the National Park Service.

storyline.headline: USGS Monitors Ongoing Kīlauea Summit Eruption with UAS Survey and Episode 29 Fountaining
storyline.summary: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory conducted a drone survey of the Kīlauea summit eruption site on July 17, followed by Episode 29 of sustained lava fountaining at Halemaʻumaʻu, which ended after over 13 hours on July 20, 2025.

storyline.headline: DOJ Drops Biden-Era Lawsuit Against Tennessee's Minor Transgender Care Ban
storyline.summary: The Justice Department's Civil Rights Division dismissed with prejudice a Biden-era lawsuit that had challenged Tennessee's law restricting sex-change medical procedures for minors, stating the challenge did not serve the public interest.

storyline.headline: Rubio Meets Philippine President Marcos Amid Trump White House Visit
storyline.summary: Secretary of State Rubio held meetings with Philippine President Marcos Jr. in Washington, culminating in a joint meeting and lunch with President Trump, reaffirming the US-Philippines alliance.

storyline.headline: Youth Conservation Corps Repairs Picnic Areas at Big South Fork
storyline.summary: Youth Conservation Corps students completed repairs on four picnic areas at Big South Fork National River & Recreation Area, per NPS.

storyline.headline: USDA Announces $675.9 Million in Disaster Aid for Florida Farmers
storyline.summary: Secretary Rollins announced $675.9 million in disaster assistance for farmers in Florida.

storyline.headline: Utah Man Pleads Guilty to Threatening Palestinian Rights Group
storyline.summary: Kevin Brent Buchanan pleaded guilty to transmitting a threatening interstate communication targeting employees of a D.C.-based Palestinian rights organization; sentencing set for Nov. 18.

storyline.headline: Senate Confirms John Hurley as Treasury Under Secretary for Terrorism and Financial Intelligence
storyline.summary: The U.S. Senate confirmed John Hurley to lead Treasury's terrorism and financial intelligence office, a role focused on combating illicit financial actors.

storyline.headline: US-Suriname Partnership
storyline.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke with Suriname President Jennifer Geerlings-Simons to congratulate her on her election and discuss strengthening the US-Suriname partnership. They aimed to support security cooperation, energy security, and regional stability.

storyline.headline: FDA Halts Sarepta Gene Therapy Distribution and Trials
storyline.summary: The FDA has suspended distribution of Elevidys and placed clinical trials for Sarepta's gene therapy products on hold due to safety concerns following 3 deaths. This decision affects multiple gene therapy products for limb girdle muscular dystrophy.

storyline.headline: NASA Confirms Betelgeuse Has Long-Predicted Companion Star
storyline.summary: NASA researchers confirmed a century-old hypothesis that Betelgeuse has a close companion star, publishing findings in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

storyline.headline: Trump Administration Secures Australian Market Access for U.S. Beef Exports
storyline.summary: The White House announced that trade negotiations resulted in expanded access for American beef exports into the Australian market, framed as a win for U.S. agriculture.

storyline.headline: Veterans Wheelchair Games Conclude in Minneapolis
storyline.summary: The 44th National Veterans Wheelchair Games wrapped up after six days of competition and camaraderie among veteran athletes in Minneapolis.

storyline.headline: USGS Coastal and Ocean Science Briefs
storyline.summary: USGS released a June-July 2025 news brief roundup covering coastal and ocean science research from across the agency.

storyline.headline: FDA Names George Tidmarsh Director of Center for Drug Evaluation and Research
storyline.summary: The FDA appointed Stanford faculty member George Tidmarsh, M.D., Ph.D., as Director of the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER).

storyline.headline: Rubio Presses Iraqi PM on Attacks on Energy Infrastructure
storyline.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke with Iraqi Prime Minister al-Sudani about recent attacks on energy infrastructure, including facilities operated by U.S. companies, urging accountability and prevention of future attacks.

storyline.headline: US Marks Egypt's National Day with Diplomatic Message
storyline.summary: The US State Department issued a congratulatory statement to Egypt on its national day, highlighting longstanding bilateral ties and cooperation on regional stability.

storyline.headline: IRS BTA Designated Officials Face Revalidation Deadline
storyline.summary: The IRS reminded Business Tax Account Designated Officials they must revalidate their accounts by July 31, 2025 or lose access to the system.

storyline.headline: Education Dept. Releases NSLDS Delinquent Borrower Report on Institutional Nonpayment Rates
storyline.summary: The Department of Education issued a default prevention resource detailing nonpayment rates by institution via the NSLDS Delinquent Borrower Report.

storyline.headline: NASA-ISRO NISAR Satellite to Monitor Earth's Land and Ice Surfaces
storyline.summary: NASA and India's ISRO launched a new joint satellite, NISAR, designed to provide high-resolution radar data on Earth's surface changes, aiding crop management, hazard monitoring, and tracking of sea ice and glaciers.

storyline.headline: NASA Extends Deadline for Moon, Mars Communications Industry Proposals
storyline.summary: NASA is soliciting proposals from U.S. companies for Moon and Mars relay communication and navigation capabilities, extending the response deadline to Sept. 17, 2025.

storyline.headline: USCIS Reaches Fiscal Year 2026 H-1B Cap
storyline.summary: The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has reached the congressionally mandated 65,000 H-1B visa regular cap and the 20,000 H-1B visa U.S. advanced degree exemption for fiscal year 2026. This means that no more new H-1B visa petitions will be accepted for the fiscal year.

storyline.headline: NASA Glenn's GVIS Lab Highlighted for Visualization Legacy
storyline.summary: NASA Glenn's Scientific Computing and Visualization Team's GVIS Lab is noted for its long-standing history in visual and technological innovation.

storyline.headline: Colorado Man Pleads Guilty to Child Exploitation Charges
storyline.summary: A Colorado man pleaded guilty to sexually exploiting a minor and possessing child sexual abuse material.

storyline.headline: USDA Launches Week-Long 'Great American Farmers Market' Celebration
storyline.summary: Secretary Rollins announced a weeklong event celebrating American agriculture through the Great American Farmers Market initiative.

storyline.headline: Steamtown Visitor Center Reopens for Summer Season
storyline.summary: The Steamtown National Historic Site visitor center reopened for the summer season, resuming normal visitor services.

storyline.headline: Lake Powell Water Levels to Impact Launch Ramps
storyline.summary: The National Park Service issued an updated forecast for Lake Powell water levels at Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, warning that changing lake levels will affect boat launch ramp availability.

storyline.headline: USGS publishes first lunar mineral prospectivity map for NASA
storyline.summary: The U.S. Geological Survey released its first off-planet mineral prospectivity map, identifying likely locations of ice near the Lunar South Pole to support a NASA mission.

storyline.headline: FTC Refunds Victims of Student Loan Forgiveness Scam
storyline.summary: The FTC distributed payments to consumers who were harmed by a deceptive student loan forgiveness scheme.

storyline.headline: NASA's GRUVE Lab supports virtual mission exploration
storyline.summary: NASA's GRUVE Lab, part of the GVIS Lab, houses the CAVE virtual reality system used for mission scenarios and touring virtual environments of NASA facilities.

storyline.headline: USBR Launches Challenge for Rapid Reservoir Seal Fix
storyline.summary: The Bureau of Reclamation is soliciting designs for a rapid-deploying temporary seal to stop uncontrolled water flow from reservoir conduits that cannot be closed.

storyline.headline: EPA Proposes Cleanup Plan for Contaminated Groundwater Superfund Site
storyline.summary: The US Environmental Protection Agency proposed a final cleanup plan for contaminated groundwater at the Fulton Avenue Superfund site in New York. The plan aims to address the site's pollution issues.

storyline.headline: State Department Investigates Harvard's Exchange Visitor Program Eligibility
storyline.summary: The U.S. Department of State has opened an investigation into whether Harvard University remains eligible to sponsor the Exchange Visitor Program, citing compliance and transparency requirements.

storyline.headline: CFTC Staff Issues No-Action Letter on Event Contracts
storyline.summary: CFTC staff issued a no-action letter addressing regulatory treatment of event contracts, providing relief or clarity to market participants offering these products.

storyline.headline: U.S. Leads Global Maritime Security Conference
storyline.summary: The U.S. Department of State co-hosted a global conference on maritime security and sanctions enforcement in Abidjan, aiming to strengthen due diligence practices and enhance sanctions enforcement. The event brought together industry leaders from 25 countries.

storyline.headline: Registration Open for Area of Concern Cross-Agency Partnership Summit
storyline.summary: The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Ohio Lake Erie Commission have opened registration for the 2025 Areas of Concern (AOC) Cross-Agency Partnership Summit, to be held September 16-18, 2025, in Toledo, Ohio. The summit aims to bring together stakeholders to discuss areas of concern.

storyline.headline: Florida Man Sentenced to 5 Years for Decades-Long IRS Fraud Scheme
storyline.summary: A Miami man received a 60-month prison sentence for conspiring to defraud the IRS by hiding millions in undisclosed Swiss bank accounts and falsely attributing the assets to foreign nationals.

storyline.headline: NASA Tests New Heat Source Fuel for Deep Space Missions
storyline.summary: NASA is testing a new radioisotope heat source fuel intended to power spacecraft on deep space missions, building on decades of RPS technology used in missions like Voyager and Perseverance.

storyline.headline: DOJ Releases 230,000 Pages of Files on MLK Assassination
storyline.summary: The Department of Justice, under Attorney General Pamela Bondi, released roughly 230,000 pages of documents related to the assassination of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., fulfilling Executive Order 14176. Bondi hosted Dr. Alveda King to commemorate the release.

storyline.headline: AI improves detection of small earthquakes at Yellowstone
storyline.summary: AI-based methods are being used to help calculate magnitudes of small, rapid seismic events at Yellowstone, addressing a longstanding measurement challenge.

storyline.headline: USPS Celebrates 250th Anniversary with Stamps and Events
storyline.summary: The U.S. Postal Service is marking its 250th founding anniversary on July 26 with special events, merchandise, and the unveiling of two new commemorative stamps.

storyline.headline: USGS Maps Southeast Geology to Aid Mineral Exploration and Safety
storyline.summary: A USGS geologic mapping project in the southeastern U.S. aims to identify critical mineral deposits and assess earthquake risks, supporting both resource development and public safety.

storyline.headline: NASA's Deep-Space Fix Saves Juno's JunoCam Near Jupiter
storyline.summary: NASA revealed that its Juno mission team used an experimental annealing technique in December 2023 to repair the radiation-damaged JunoCam imager, enabling it to capture images of Jupiter's moon Io. The success offers insights that could benefit other spacecraft facing high-radiation environments.

storyline.headline: US Employment Update
storyline.summary: The US government released a monthly news release on state employment and unemployment, providing an update on the current job market.

storyline.headline: Hawai‘i Volcanoes National Park August 2025 Events
storyline.summary: Hawai‘i Volcanoes National Park has announced events and updates for August 2025. The park is providing information on upcoming activities and changes through the US National Park Service.

storyline.headline: Rubio's Daily Schedule Includes Meeting with Jordanian FM
storyline.summary: The State Department released Secretary Rubio's July 23, 2025 public schedule, noting a meeting with Jordanian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi.

storyline.headline: Blue Ridge Parkway Reopens 12-Mile Stretch After Road Project
storyline.summary: The National Park Service completed a road project reopening a 12-mile corridor of the Blue Ridge Parkway between Blowing Rock and Linville Falls, North Carolina.

storyline.headline: NCBI to Roll Out ClinVar Search Interface Upgrades
storyline.summary: NCBI announced upcoming enhancements to ClinVar's homepage and search experience, including a new multi-box search interface for entering multiple terms.

storyline.headline: Young Mob Gang Members Indicted in Memphis
storyline.summary: Eight members of the Young Mob gang in Memphis have been indicted on charges including racketeering, murder, robbery, and drug charges. The defendants, including Larry Wilson, have made their initial appearances in federal court.

storyline.headline: Federal EHR tool boosts early lung cancer detection for Veterans
storyline.summary: The VA's Federal EHR system, via its Comprehensive Adult Wellness Registry tool, is helping identify Veterans eligible for earlier lung cancer screenings.

storyline.headline: DOJ Backs Seattle's Bid to End Police Consent Decree
storyline.summary: The Justice Department's Civil Rights Division filed a response supporting Seattle's motion to terminate the long-standing consent decree governing SPD use-of-force, crisis intervention, and accountability reforms.

storyline.headline: Court Upholds Bureau of Reclamation's Water Contract Conversions in Central Valley
storyline.summary: A federal district court in California affirmed the Bureau of Reclamation's authority to convert water service contracts to long-term repayment contracts under the WIIN Act, eliminating renewal requirements for Central Valley water users.

storyline.headline: New Director of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services
storyline.summary: Joseph B. Edlow began serving as the director of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services after being confirmed by the United States Senate on July 15, 2025.

storyline.headline: Illinois Tax Preparer Sentenced in $3.6M COVID Relief Fraud Case
storyline.summary: An Illinois man was sentenced to 42 months in prison for orchestrating a scheme to fraudulently obtain over $3.6 million in PPP and EIDL COVID-19 relief funds.

storyline.headline: State Job Openings and Labor Turnover Report Released
storyline.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics issued its regular state-level JOLTS report, providing data on job openings and labor turnover across states.

storyline.headline: FTC Shuts Down Fake Debt-Relief Operation
storyline.summary: The FTC halted an illegal debt-relief operation that falsely impersonated businesses and the government, harming consumers. This operation was shut down on July 18, 2025.

storyline.headline: NASA Tests Super Cold Fuel Storage Technique
storyline.summary: NASA is testing an innovative technique for storing super cold fuel in space, where temperatures can drop to minus 455 degrees Fahrenheit. The technique aims to preserve ultra-cold fluid propellants from overheating due to onboard systems, solar radiation, and spacecraft exhaust.

storyline.headline: Rubio Discusses State Department Overhaul in Fox News Interview
storyline.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio sat down with Lara Trump of Fox News to discuss restructuring and cutbacks at the State Department, calling the changes long overdue.

storyline.headline: State Department Releases Daily Public Schedule
storyline.summary: The U.S. Department of State published its routine daily public schedule for July 24, 2025, noting Secretary Rubio's meeting with Austria's Foreign Minister and Deputy Secretary Landau's activities.

storyline.headline: Leader of Nationwide Catalytic Converter Theft Ring Pleads Guilty in $600M Scheme
storyline.summary: The leader of a national catalytic converter theft ring pleaded guilty, admitting to selling stolen catalytic converters for more than $600 million.

storyline.headline: Education Dept Issues FISAP Reporting Reminders for 2024–25/2026–27
storyline.summary: A federal bulletin (CB-25-12) reminds institutions of information and reporting requirements for the Fiscal Operations Report for 2024–25 and the Application to Participate for 2026–27 (FISAP).

storyline.headline: New 3DEP Fact Sheet Highlights Lidar Data for Louisiana
storyline.summary: USGS released a new fact sheet detailing how 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) lidar data supports Louisiana's economy.

storyline.headline: EPA Announces Reduction in Force and Reorganization
storyline.summary: The US Environmental Protection Agency announced a reduction in force and reorganization efforts to save taxpayers nearly $749 million. This move is part of the agency's comprehensive restructuring efforts.

storyline.headline: USCIS Updates Fees Based on H.R. 1
storyline.summary: The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has updated its fees based on the H.R. 1 Reconciliation Bill. This change was published in a federal register notice.

storyline.headline: EPA Completes Soil Sampling Review at Missouri School
storyline.summary: The EPA finished reviewing soil sample data collected from Davis R-12 school in Henry County, Missouri, following June 2025 sampling.

storyline.headline: US Cracks Down on Haitian Gang Ties Among Legal Residents
storyline.summary: The State Department announced deportation actions against U.S. lawful permanent residents linked to Haitian gang network Viv Ansanm, and USCIS helped ICE arrest a Haitian national accused of contributing to Haiti's destabilization.

storyline.headline: EPA Secures Vistra Cleanup Deal for Moss Landing Battery Fire Site
storyline.summary: The EPA reached an agreement with Vistra Corp. to safely remove and dispose of batteries damaged in the January 2025 fire at Moss Landing, and launched a website for public updates.

storyline.headline: NASA Trials Mixed Reality Tech in Flight Simulator
storyline.summary: NASA is testing a mixed reality system combining physical flight simulators with VR headsets to create a more immersive, affordable pilot training tool.

storyline.headline: Des Moines Man Indicted on Sex Trafficking Charges
storyline.summary: A federal grand jury in the Northern District of Iowa unsealed an eight-count indictment against a Des Moines man for sex trafficking by force, fraud or coercion, and interstate transportation for prostitution.

storyline.headline: Rubio Discusses Regional Stability, Economic Reforms with Ethiopian PM Abiy
storyline.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke with Ethiopian PM Abiy Ahmed about stability in the Horn of Africa and Ethiopia's economic reforms, which could boost U.S. trade and investment ties.

storyline.headline: DOJ Releases Records to Senate Judiciary Committee on Clinton Email Probe
storyline.summary: The Department of Justice, under Attorney General Pamela Bondi, honored a request from Senate Judiciary Chairman Chuck Grassley for information on the FBI's handling of the Hillary Clinton email investigation.

storyline.headline: US Unseals Forfeiture Action Against $2M in Crypto Tied to Hamas Fundraising
storyline.summary: The Justice Department unsealed a civil forfeiture action targeting roughly $2 million in digital currency held on Tether and Binance linked to a Gaza-based money transfer firm accused of funding Hamas.

storyline.headline: Old Report on Goosenest Volcano's 'Hot Springs' Debunked
storyline.summary: A historical claim by volcanologist Howell Williams about hot springs on Goosenest volcano in northern California has been reexamined and found questionable.

storyline.headline: Frank Pagliocca's Rehabilitation Journey
storyline.summary: Frank Pagliocca underwent detox, therapy, and rehabilitation with the help of mental health professionals, eventually finding healing and stability. This journey showcases a personal struggle and recovery process.

storyline.headline: State Department Marks Belgium's National Day
storyline.summary: The U.S. Department of State issued a congratulatory statement to Belgium on its National Day, highlighting shared NATO membership and commitment to security cooperation.

storyline.headline: Navy Veteran Honored Through Final Mile Ceremony Program
storyline.summary: A Navy veteran with no next of kin was honored in a Final Mile Ceremony, a program designed to ensure such veterans are not forgotten upon their passing.

storyline.headline: US, Japan, and South Korea Strengthen Trilateral Partnership
storyline.summary: Deputy Secretary of State Landau met with Japanese Vice Foreign Minister Funakoshi and ROK First Vice Foreign Minister Park to advance the trilateral partnership, focusing on safety, security, and prosperity. The meeting aimed to strengthen cooperation between the three countries.

storyline.headline: Honoring Veterans: Army Veteran Edna Cummings
storyline.summary: The US government honored Army Veteran Edna Cummings for her 25-year service in a recent spotlight feature.

storyline.headline: Newark Roofing Contractor Settles for $155K Over Safety Violations
storyline.summary: The US Department of Labor reached a settlement with a Newark roofing contractor affirming a $155,000 penalty for multiple violations.

storyline.headline: CFTC Extends No-Action Letter on Position Aggregation
storyline.summary: The CFTC staff has issued an extension of a no-action letter regarding position aggregation requirements, initially announced on July 18, 2025.

storyline.headline: VA Expands Healthcare in Nevada
storyline.summary: The VA has partnered with local academic institutions to bring more doctors to Nevada, improving healthcare for Veterans and nearby communities. This partnership ensures the presence of essential health professionals in the area.

storyline.headline: Importers Pay $6.8M to Settle False Claims Act Customs Duty Case
storyline.summary: Global Plastics LLC and Marco Polo International LLC, subsidiaries of MGI International LLC, agreed to pay $6.8 million to resolve civil liability under the False Claims Act for knowingly avoiding customs duties on plastic resin imports from China. The settlement followed a voluntary self-disclosure by the companies.

storyline.headline: Fort Raleigh Seeks Public Input on Shoreline Stabilization Plan
storyline.summary: Fort Raleigh National Historic Site opened a public comment period on a proposal to stabilize its eroding shoreline.

storyline.headline: IRS Offers Help for Taxpayers Who Missed April Deadline
storyline.summary: The IRS issued a reminder to taxpayers who missed the April filing deadline that assistance is still available to help them file late.

storyline.headline: US Rejects 2024 Amendments to International Health Regulations
storyline.summary: The US has rejected the 2024 amendments to the International Health Regulations (2005), fulfilling a promise to protect American interests in the international system. This decision was made in collaboration with the Department of Health and Human Services.

storyline.headline: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-11 Mission
storyline.summary: NASA's SpaceX Crew-11 mission is set to launch four crew members to the International Space Station for research and maintenance activities. The mission aims to perform various research, technology demonstrations, and maintenance tasks aboard the orbiting laboratory.

storyline.headline: Five Nevada Men Sentenced for Running Jetflicks Illegal Streaming Service
storyline.summary: Five Nevada men, including a German citizen, received final judgments for operating Jetflicks, one of the largest illegal TV streaming services in the US, with sentences up to 84 months in prison.

storyline.headline: USGS Biologist Kauffman Wins 2024 Aldo Leopold Conservation Award
storyline.summary: Dr. Matthew Kauffman, a USGS Research Wildlife Biologist and Unit Leader of the Wyoming Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Research Unit, received the 2024 Aldo Leopold Conservation Award, as detailed in a nomination letter released by the American Society of Mammalogists.

storyline.headline: Lower Neponset River Superfund Site Presentation
storyline.summary: The EPA has scheduled a presentation for the Lower Neponset River Superfund Site on July 22, 2025. This event is part of the EPA's efforts to address environmental concerns in the area.

storyline.headline: Waste Management Company Cited After Worker Dies in Confined Space Incident
storyline.summary: Federal investigators cited a waste management company for failing to implement required confined space entry procedures, which resulted in a worker's death.

storyline.headline: Low-level flights to image geology over Black Hills, Bear Lodge area
storyline.summary: Low-level airplane flights are set to begin over the Black Hills and Bear Lodge areas of Wyoming and South Dakota to image geology using airborne geophysical technology. The flights are scheduled to start as soon as late July.

storyline.headline: US Imposes Visa Restrictions on Brazilian Judicial Officials
storyline.summary: The US has imposed visa restrictions on Brazilian judicial officials and their families due to censorship of protected expression in the US, specifically targeting those involved in a political witch hunt against Jair Bolsonaro. This move aims to hold foreign nationals accountable for violating basic rights of Brazilians.

storyline.headline: Engineer Pleads Guilty to Stealing Missile Tech Trade Secrets for China
storyline.summary: An engineer pleaded guilty to stealing trade secret technology designed for missile launch and detection, intending to benefit the Chinese government.

storyline.headline: FTC and DOJ Hold Joint Session on Drug Price Competition
storyline.summary: The FTC and DOJ's Antitrust Division, with Commerce and HHS, held a listening session focused on lowering drug prices through increased market competition.

storyline.headline: NPS Releases 2025 Battle of the Crater Anniversary Schedule
storyline.summary: The National Park Service published its 2025 program schedule for the Battle of the Crater Anniversary at Petersburg National Battlefield.

storyline.headline: DOJ Sentences Managers of Dark Web CSAM Site in Operation Grayskull
storyline.summary: The Justice Department announced results of Operation Grayskull, a joint DOJ-FBI effort that dismantled four dark web sites hosting child sexual abuse material, leading to 18 convictions including lengthy sentences for site managers.

storyline.headline: VA Explores Rural Communities
storyline.summary: The US Department of Veterans Affairs is exploring opportunities in rural communities, such as the facility in Bath, New York. This initiative aims to discover new career paths at rural VA facilities.

storyline.headline: VA Highlights Homeownership Benefits for Veterans
storyline.summary: The VA published a piece emphasizing how homeownership fosters stability, wealth-building, and purpose for veterans and their families.

storyline.headline: Justice Department Proposes Rule to Restore Firearms Rights
storyline.summary: The Justice Department has published a proposed rule to grant relief to certain individuals precluded from possessing firearms due to past convictions, aiming to address Second Amendment rights infringements. This move follows President Trump's direction to the Department of Justice to address these infringements.

storyline.headline: US Welcomes Declaration of Principles between DRC and Congo River Alliance
storyline.summary: The US welcomed the signing of a Declaration of Principles between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and representatives of Congo River Alliance, facilitated by Qatar. This step aims to advance lasting peace in the region.

storyline.headline: NASA Tests Scalable Satellite Tech
storyline.summary: NASA launched the Athena EPIC satellite to test scalable satellite technology, aiming to launch sensors quicker. The satellite was launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

storyline.headline: FTC Seeks Comment on Petition to Vacate 2021 Order Related to Stalkerware Apps
storyline.summary: The Federal Trade Commission is seeking public comment on a request to vacate or modify the FTC's order banning monitoring apps. The request comes from the CEO of a company that marketed 'stalkerware' apps.

storyline.headline: VA Expands Menopause Support for Women Veterans
storyline.summary: The VA highlighted resources for women veterans navigating menopause, including medication, whole health counseling, and lifestyle support.

storyline.headline: MS-13 Members Sentenced for Racketeering in Massachusetts
storyline.summary: Two MS-13 members were sentenced in federal court in Boston for their roles in a previously unsolved murder, highlighting the ongoing efforts to combat gang violence. The sentencing is part of a broader crackdown on MS-13 activities in the US.

storyline.headline: DOJ Forms Strike Force to Assess ODNI Gabbard's Disclosed Evidence
storyline.summary: The Justice Department announced a new Strike Force to review evidence made public by Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard and determine potential legal next steps.

storyline.headline: Two Mexican Nationals Sentenced in Multimillion-Dollar Money Laundering Scheme
storyline.summary: Two Mexican nationals were sentenced to 55 months each in federal prison for their roles in a two-year trade-based money laundering conspiracy that moved drug trafficking proceeds from Texas to Mexico.

storyline.headline: US-Djibouti Strategic Partnership Discussed
storyline.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke with Djiboutian President Ismail Omar Guelleh about the US-Djibouti strategic partnership and maintaining peace in the Red Sea and Horn of Africa. The discussion highlights the importance of the relationship between the two countries.

storyline.headline: NPS Feature on Historic Lakeside Cottages at Johnstown Flood Memorial
storyline.summary: The National Park Service published an informational piece about historic cottages at the Johnstown Flood National Memorial as part of its 'Evening on the Lake' series.

storyline.headline: NASA's Tracking and Data Relay Satellites (TDRS)
storyline.summary: NASA's TDRS have provided near-continuous, high-bandwidth communications to over 25 missions in low Earth orbit for more than 40 years. The TDRS fleet transmits signals between ground stations, spacecraft, and other relays.

storyline.headline: NJ Construction Company Owner Sentenced for Tax Evasion
storyline.summary: A New Jersey construction company owner was sentenced to 15 months in prison for evading employment tax penalties assessed against him.
